desc: Two notes, Bb3 -> G3: the descending minor third, the classic 'sigh' interval. The second note is longer, softer and dies away with slow wide vibrato.
One long sigh: a small lift (the in-breath), then a continuous slide down more than an octave, 300 -> 115 Hz, breathy, wide slow vibrato, amplitude dying away.
The lament bass: four steps down the minor scale, Bb3 Ab3 Gb3 F3 (1, b7, b6, 5 in Bb minor), each note softer and slower than the last, the final note held and fading.
Reach and collapse: a leap UP a minor sixth (Bb3 -> Gb4, the 'yearning' interval), held a moment with trembling vibrato, then one slow slide down past the start to F3.
A whimper: one low note (G3) drifting downward, with two sob-catches (short dips in the loudness like a caught breath) and a tremor that widens and slows as the sound dies.
Three notes falling down a G minor triad, D4 Bb3 G3, each one slower and quieter (ritardando + diminuendo): a phrase that runs out of energy.
QUACK QUACK: two short hard hits at 320 Hz (above the centre), instant attack with a click, rasp AM at 28 Hz, crackle; the second hit is louder and a touch higher.
Three accelerating stabs climbing a minor second each time (D4 Eb4 E4): the tightest, most dissonant step in the scale, repeated, faster and louder each time.
Tritone stabs: Bb3 up to E4 (the tritone, the 'devil's interval'), back to Bb3. Three hits, the last one held longer and chopped off flat, no decay tail.
A low growl (150 Hz, full-depth rasp at 24 Hz, crackle) swelling and rising over 0.8 s into one loud bark at 360 Hz that stops dead.
Flat-then-chopped: a held rasp at 300 Hz for 0.4 s, then the same note chopped by a hard 8 Hz gate into a machine-gun 'ka-ka-ka-ka-ka' that rises slightly and ends on the loudest chop.
A snarl: fast trill between E4 and F4 (a minor second, 12 alternations per second) over a full-depth rasp, then one hard bark a tritone below (Bb3) that cuts off.
